title: Dividing by zero
summary: Why `total / 0` compiles without a warning but crashes when it runs, and how to check the divisor before dividing.
objectives: Explain why `int total = 90; int average = total / 0;` compiles but throws an exception when it runs.
Trace a division expression and identify when the program reaches a zero divisor.
Check a divisor before dividing and handle the zero case.
Recognize the same risk when the divisor is a variable or is used with `%`.

blocks.text: This is exactly the mistake Code Coach flags: the program tries to divide an `int` by zero.

`javac` accepts this statement without an error or a warning, even though the `0` is written right there in the code. Even `10 / 0` compiles. When the program runs and reaches `total / 0`, Java throws an `ArithmeticException`. This is a run-time error, not a compile-time error.

blocks.title: The important detail
blocks.text: For `int` division, the number on the right of `/` is the divisor. It must not be zero. In the flagged code, the divisor is the literal `0`.

Java evaluates the division when it reaches that statement. It can read the value `90` from `total`, but it cannot calculate an `int` result for `total / 0`. The statement throws an exception instead of storing a value in `average`.

blocks.caption: Check the divisor before calculating an average
blocks.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  A[Start with total and count] --> B{Is count zero}
  B -- yes --> C[Do not divide]
  C --> D[Handle the missing average]
  B -- no --> E[Calculate total divided by count]
  E --> F[Use the average]

blocks.text: For the flagged code, the divisor is the literal `0`, so there is no useful check to perform: the statement itself needs to change. In an average calculation, the divisor is usually a variable such as `count`. Check that variable before using it.

blocks.text: The chart shows results for positive counts. If `count` is `0`, there is no integer result to put in the chart: the division throws an exception.

sections.title: Trace it, one step at a time

blocks.text: A trace lists what Java does in order. Follow the flagged code from the declaration to the division.

blocks.caption: Tracing `int total = 90; int average = total / 0;`
rows: Java creates `total` and stores `90` in it.
Java starts evaluating the right side before assigning a value to `average`.
Java reads `total` as `90` and finds that the divisor is `0`.
Java throws `ArithmeticException`; the assignment to `average` does not finish.

blocks.text: The error occurs at step 3, when the program runs. The compiler gives no error or warning for it.
For an average, the count is the divisor. First decide what the program should do when the count is zero. Only calculate the average in the other case.
Here `count` is `3`, so the `else` branch runs. Java calculates `90 / 3` and stores `30` in `average`. If `count` were `0`, the first branch would run and the division would be skipped.

This example still checks for zero first. The cast `(double) total` makes the division produce a decimal result. Without that cast, `90 / 4` would be integer division and give `22`, because Java discards the fractional part when both operands are `int`.
The flagged code writes `0` directly. Often the zero comes from a variable instead, so the danger is less obvious. The variable still needs checking before the division.

good.title: Check before dividing

blocks.note: The first statement compiles, but if `count` is `0` when it runs, it throws `ArithmeticException`. The second version handles that case before evaluating `total / count`.

good.title: Check the divisor for remainder too

blocks.note: The `%` operator gives a remainder, but an `int` remainder operation also throws `ArithmeticException` if its divisor is `0`. Check the divisor before using `%`.

blocks.question: In the flagged code, when does `total / 0` cause a problem?
options: The compiler rejects the code before it can run.
The code compiles, then throws an exception when the division runs.
blocks.explanation: Java does not check for a zero divisor when it compiles, even a literal `0`, so this compiles. At run time, the `int` division reaches a divisor of `0` and throws `ArithmeticException`.

blocks.question: Which version avoids dividing when `count` is zero?
blocks.explanation: The `else` branch runs only when `count == 0` is false. That means `total / count` is not evaluated when `count` is zero.

blocks.question: What does `90 / 4` produce when both values are `int`?
blocks.explanation: Both operands are `int`, so Java discards the fractional part. The result is `22`. This is integer division, not division by zero.

items: The flagged code `int average = total / 0;` compiles without a warning, then throws `ArithmeticException` when the division runs.
A zero divisor is a run-time problem for this `int` division, not a compile-time warning.
For an average, check that `count` is not `0` before calculating `total / count`.
A variable can hold zero even when the code does not show a literal `0`; check its value before dividing.
Use the same zero-divisor check before an `int` remainder operation with `%`.
When both operands are `int`, division discards the fractional part. Use a floating-point operand when a decimal result is needed.
